data.gender_notes: Surabhi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Surabhi is a name derived from Sanskrit language. It is a divine cow, who is considered the giver of all pleasures and the embodiment of prosperity. According to Hindu mythology, she is the mother of all cows and the one who nourishes the gods and the universe. Surabhi's name is also associated with the fragrant flowers of the Kadamb tree, symbolizing purity, abundance, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the abundant and nourishing power of nature and the divine grace that bestows prosperity and happiness.
data.etymology: Surabhi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Abundance, Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Surabhi total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Surabhi is a revered deity and symbolic representation of abundance and prosperity in Hindu culture. She is often depicted as a beautiful, large-eyed, white cow standing on a lotus with four hands, each holding a lotus, a rosary, and a vessel of liquid offering. The image of Surabhi is a common motif in Indian art, temples, and literature, reflecting her importance in Hindu mythology and traditional beliefs. She is also mentioned in various Hindu scriptures like the Vedas and the Puranas, signifying her role in preserving and disseminating the spiritual knowledge of Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: Surabhi represents selfless giving, unconditional love, and generosity in Hindu spirituality. As a divine cow, she is a giver of all pleasures and is believed to provide nourishment to the soul. Moreover, Surabhi is considered a divine mother who offers her milk to all, signifying unconditional love and compassion towards all beings. Her name is also associated with the Kadamb flowers, representing the purity and fragrance of the soul. Surabhi is a symbol of the divine feminine energy that nurtures, protects, and sustains all of creation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Surabhi, in Hindu mythology, represents the abundant, eternal, and udandishta (milk-giving) cow. She is a symbol of wealth, prosperity, and nourishment, embodying the maternal and creative aspects of the universe.

vedic_reference.note: The name Surabhi is mentioned in the Rigveda and Mahabharata. Surabhi is a divine cow, the mother of all cows, and the source of all milk and sustenance for the gods. She is described as having a thousand teats and is considered to be the embodiment of prosperity and abundance.

historical_references.reference: Surabhi, also known as the 'Cows of the Gods,' was a celestial cow in Hindu mythology. She is said to have given birth to all the rivers and provided sustenance to the gods.
historical_references.time_period: Pre-Vedic to Classical Period (circa 2500 BCE to 500 CE)

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Surabhi comes from the Ramayana, where she is described as the mother of all cows and the wife of the divine sage Vedavyasa. She is also believed to have given the divine nectar, Amrita, to the gods during the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan).
